zion.title: Zion National Park: Canyon Travel, Shuttles and Trail Planning
zion.deck: The most useful first decision is how you will enter Zion Canyon and what kind of hike matches your group. Plan for shuttle operations, permitted sections, river hazards and time in Springdale.

blocks.p: Zion states that regular park entry and rides on its park shuttle do not require an advance reservation or shuttle ticket. Visitors still need a valid entrance pass or must pay the park entrance fee. Shuttle service and schedules change seasonally, so confirm the operating dates and plan around stop locations.

The chain-supported section from Scout Lookout to Angels Landing requires an Angels Landing hiking permit. Hiking to Scout Lookout by the West Rim Trail does not require that specific permit, although the approach is strenuous and conditions still matter.

blocks.h: The Narrows: choose the correct route
blocks.p: The common bottom-up approach from the Temple of Sinawava does not require a wilderness permit within its allowed upstream boundary. The long top-down route from Chamberlain’s Ranch does require a permit. Flash flooding and river conditions can close routes with little notice.

faq: Do I need a reservation to enter Zion National Park?
NPS says no general entrance reservation or shuttle ticket is required; an entrance pass or fee is still required. Special activities can have their own permits.
https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm
Do I need a permit for Angels Landing?
Yes for the chain section beyond Scout Lookout. The approach to Scout Lookout itself does not require that particular permit.
https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm
Is The Narrows hike always open?
No. Flood risk, high river flow and other changing hazards affect access. Always check the official conditions on the day of your visit.
https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/planning-guide.htm

great-smoky-mountains.title: Great Smoky Mountains: Trailheads, Shuttles and Parking
great-smoky-mountains.deck: Access choices matter in the Smokies: popular trailhead lots fill, parking tags do not reserve spaces, and guided gateway transportation can reduce parking stress.

blocks.h: Parking tags and scarce trailhead spaces
blocks.p: A valid parking tag does not guarantee a parking space. NPS points to busy trailheads and overlooks with limited capacity and recommends planning around demand rather than assuming a tag creates a reservation.

blocks.h: Getting to trails and popular viewpoints
blocks.p: Shuttle operators are listed by NPS as transportation options in the region. Confirm a provider’s departure location, availability, accessibility and fees independently before planning a route.

blocks.h: Build an itinerary across both states
blocks.p: Great Smoky Mountains spans Tennessee and North Carolina. Travelers should choose a gateway and driving route deliberately instead of assuming every trail or attraction is close to the same entrance.

faq: Does a Smokies parking tag reserve a space?
No. A parking tag does not guarantee a particular spot, and popular trailhead lots may fill.
https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/shuttles.htm
Can I use a shuttle around the Smokies?
The NPS lists regional shuttle services; confirm each operator’s routes and current terms directly.
https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/shuttles.htm

yellowstone.title: Yellowstone: Geysers, Wildlife and Safe Exploration
yellowstone.deck: Yellowstone combines multiple geographic regions, active geothermal systems and wild animals. Plan by entrance and travel time, give wildlife space, and stay on the designated thermal walkways.

blocks.p: Yellowstone NPS guidance requires at least 100 yards of separation from bears, wolves and cougars, and at least 25 yards from other large animals including bison and elk. Never approach wildlife for a photo.

blocks.h: Thermal basins are not ordinary trails
blocks.p: Stay on boardwalks and marked routes around thermal features. Thin ground and scalding water are dangerous, and entering hot springs is prohibited.
Yellowstone lies across Wyoming, Montana and Idaho and has five main entrances. Choose lodging and daily routes by region instead of assuming you can reach every attraction on a short drive.

faq: How close can I get to bison in Yellowstone?
Stay at least 25 yards away, and farther if an animal approaches. For bears, wolves and cougars, stay at least 100 yards away.
https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm
May I step off geyser boardwalks for a photo?
No. Remain on designated boardwalks and trails; fragile ground and extremely hot water can be deadly.
https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety-press.htm

glacier.title: Glacier: Going-to-the-Sun Road, Logan Pass and Shuttles
glacier.deck: Glacier’s scenic high road is seasonal and weather-dependent. In 2026, vehicle entry reservations are not required, but Logan Pass shuttle operations and parking limits require distinct planning.

blocks.p: The alpine portion of Going-to-the-Sun Road has no guaranteed annual opening date. Snow, storms and roadwork can close sections unexpectedly even in periods when the route is normally accessible.

NPS announced that vehicle reservations were not required anywhere in Glacier for the 2026 season. That is different from Logan Pass seasonal shuttle arrangements: certain shuttle service requires reservations and time-limited parking rules apply.
NPS trail status reports show known closures and hazards but cannot monitor every stretch at every moment. Prepare for rapidly shifting alpine conditions before committing to a hike.

faq: Is Going-to-the-Sun Road open year-round?
No. Lower portions may remain accessible, but the alpine section is seasonal and can close based on snowfall and weather.
https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/gtsrinfo.htm
Did Glacier require vehicle reservations in 2026?
NPS said no vehicle reservations were required in the park in 2026; certain Logan Pass shuttle services had separate reservations.
https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/glacier-national-park-remind-visitors-about-2026-shuttle-system-and-logan-pass-access-changes.htm

yosemite.title: Yosemite: Valley Access, Overnight Permits and Half Dome
yosemite.deck: Yosemite's granite scenery can be experienced in many ways, but reservations for overnight stays, wilderness travel and certain technical routes differ from park entrance requirements.

blocks.p: The National Park Service states that an entrance reservation is not required to enter Yosemite during 2026. Park fees, normal access restrictions and evolving conditions still apply.
Permits are required for Half Dome when its cables are up, and wilderness permits apply to overnight backcountry travel. These are distinct from general day entry requirements.
Overnight stays require appropriate accommodation bookings. Confirm campground or lodging availability independently and consider the travel time between lodging communities and valley destinations.

faq: Do I need a reservation simply to enter Yosemite in 2026?
No general entrance reservation is required according to NPS, but special activities and stays still have separate requirements.
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm
Do I need a permit to hike Half Dome?
Yes when the cables are up. An overnight wilderness permit does not automatically eliminate the Half Dome permit requirement.
https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm
